name: Ben Bowman

bio.statement: His official legislative biography says he works as a school district administrator.
bio.excerpt: In his day job, he works as a school district administrator.

bio.statement: His official biography says he earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Oregon and a master's degree from Stanford University.
bio.excerpt: he earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Oregon and his master's degree from Stanford University.

bio.statement: His official biography says he represents House District 25, covering Tigard, Metzger and South Beaverton.
bio.excerpt: representing House District 25 (Tigard, Metzger, and South Beaverton).

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Bowman lists his occupation as senior fellow at Lewis & Clark College and House Majority Leader, with a background as a Gladstone school district administrator and Oregon Department of Education policy analyst.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Senior Fellow, Lewis & Clark College; Majority Leader of the Oregon House of Representatives Occupational Background: School District Administrator, Gladstone School District; Policy Analyst, Oregon Department of Education

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

bio.statement: Bowman lists an MA from Stanford University and a BA from the University of Oregon.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: MA, Stanford University; BA, University of Oregon

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: In his 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Bowman said the state must build more housing and make purchasing easier for first-time home buyers.
positions.excerpt: We must build more housing, make purchasing easier for first-time home buyers,

positions.statement: In his 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Bowman said he supports reducing healthcare and prescription drug costs and expanding affordable childcare.
positions.excerpt: I support reducing the cost of healthcare and prescription drugs, expanding affordable childcare options

positions.statement: In his March 2026 session newsletter, Bowman is quoted saying the session positioned Oregon as a national leader on standing up for immigrant communities.
positions.excerpt: The work that we did this session has positioned Oregon as a national leader on standing up for our immigrant communities.

positions.statement: His March 2026 newsletter quotes Bowman on a home-buying bill, saying Oregonians should not be competing with Wall Street to buy a home.
positions.excerpt: The premise of this bill is simple: Oregonians should not be competing with Wall Street to buy a home.

positions.statement: Bowman cites voting to cut taxes for 200,000 working Oregonians under the heading of lowering costs.
positions.excerpt: Lowering Your Costs: Ben voted to cut taxes for 200,000 working Oregonians.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Bowman cites passing a law barring corporations and private equity from controlling physician practices.
positions.excerpt: Keeping Healthcare Local: Ben passed a first-in-the-nation law barring corporations and private equity from controlling physician practices

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Bowman says he supports a well-funded, outcomes-oriented education system.
positions.excerpt: Improving Our Schools: Ben is a champion for a well-funded, outcomes-oriented education system.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Bowman cites backing laws protecting Oregonians' due process and privacy rights against federal immigration enforcement.
positions.excerpt: He backed laws protecting Oregonians' due process and privacy rights against federal immigration enforcement.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Bowman cites votes for stronger penalties for fentanyl dealing, removing the statute of limitations for child sexual abuse and increasing punishment for domestic violence.
positions.excerpt: Making Oregon Safer: Ben voted for stronger penalties for those dealing fentanyl, removing the statute of limitations for child sexual abuse, and increasing the punishment for domestic violence.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

positions.statement: Bowman cites supporting record investments in affordable housing and speeding up permitting for housing construction.
positions.excerpt: Addressing Homelessness, Building Housing: Ben supported record investments in affordable housing.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 44

voting_record.statement: His March 2026 newsletter says Bowman was lead author of Senate Bill 951, a 2025 law on the corporate practice of medicine.
voting_record.excerpt: was lead author of Senate Bill 951, a 2025 law designed to prevent the corporate practice of medicine in Oregon.
